what: A CSS 3D cylinder with several photos (8 by default) standing around a circle, each photo split into five pieces joined with slight bends at the end of the previous piece to form a curved band — diameter --fx-d, photo width is circumference ÷ (count × 1.2), height is 2/3 of the width. Tilted X −110° · Y −15° to look up from below, and it keeps turning straight (linear) at 12° per second. It rests when off-screen and stops and resumes on the fx:pause · fx:play events. Uses CSS 3D only, no WebGL

options.segs: Number of pieces one slide is split into, default 5
options.tilt-x · tilt-y: Cylinder tilt (degrees), default −110 · −15 — the element’s own transform is left to the user (change tilt on scroll), so it is set to 0 · 0 and can also be applied directly to the element
options.--fx-radius: Rounded corners at both band ends (css), default 10px
options.[data-fx-part=photo]: One photo (child) — if background-image exists, that image is stitched across the pieces, otherwise a skin-colored placeholder panel (data-label is the name)
options.fx:pause · fx:play: Send to the element to pause and resume the loop (accessibility pause button)

note: For the cylinder to show, an ancestor needs perspective (the element itself or the wrapping panel)

from.where: index.html Hero .d3-circle(data-fx=css3d-ring-spin · tilt 0 0 — tilt and scroll movement are applied to the element by d3.js) — original css3d.js mainAnimation: _circleRotation += (elapsed ms × .012)° · css3d.css #mv01 diameter 1000px×1.2×window ratio, 8 images, --circle-img-width = Diameter×3.14/(8×1.2), height = width/3×2, five pieces (width 21% · left 95% · rotateY(angle/5.6)), rotateX(-110deg) rotateY(-15deg)
